description: We're the Lunar Cadets, a team of curious builders who love space, code and design. We're creating a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: a fun, game-style app that lets kids train for a lunar mission. We're looking for a UI/UX designer, a game or web developer, and a storyteller or science researcher. Beginners welcome. Bring your curiosity and let's launch together! 🚀
summary: Moon Base Mission Trainer is a browser game for kids aged 7 to 12 where you run a Moon base for 10 days (sols). Each sol you split limited power between an oxygen maker and a shield booster. Unused power is lost, so every choice has a cost. Real solar flares from NASA's DONKI space weather database set the storms that hit the base, and stronger storms hurt the crew unless the shield is high. After each sol the game explains what the shield blocked, and a final debrief shows what happened and why. It needs no download or account and works on a phone, so students can learn how mission planners balance power, air and radiation protection.
details:
What it does: players manage power, oxygen and shield strength on a Moon base for 10 sols, with less power during a lunar night.

How it works: the page loads solar flares from the last 30 days from NASA DONKI, turns each flare class (C, M, X) into a storm strength, and applies radiation damage reduced by shield strength. If NASA data can't load, the game says so and uses practice storms.

Benefits: kids see that no choice is free and can replay with different storms.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with animated SVG, hosted on GitHub Pages.

Limits: the radiation numbers are simplified for kids and are not yet calibrated with RadLab dose data.

Next steps: RadLab, OSDR facts, and testing with students.
